messages:
Maya: heads-up — bringing lyra-q5k (q5_k quant profile) into staging for multilang onboarding. Quick smoke shows two weird things: (1) proper-name hallucinations when translating zh->ar (person names replaced with unrelated arabic names), (2) some bracket/paren mirroring in RTL output — e.g. '(' becomes ')' or order flips. Repro below.
Maya: repro prompt:
```
zh: '李小龙访问(北京)时，记者问：他来自哪里？'
system: translate to Arabic preserving names and punctuation literally
```
Maya: fp16 baseline (lyra fp16) is clean. Issue appears after quantizing to q5_k and enabling the new kvcache-prefix opt.
Jun: can you paste the exact model hash + quant config? also the staging run id pls
Maya: model: lyra/2026-03-18-rc1, hash: 8a7f2b1c, quant: q5_k (symmetric, per-channel), extra: kvcache-prefix=on, batch=1, max_seq=512, seed=42. run: staging-lyra-8592
Liam: did we change tokenization or detok steps for the q5 pipeline? bracket mirroring smells like bidi or detok mismatch, name hallucination points to embedding/id collision after quant.
Maya: tokenization pipeline is identical to baseline: bert-ish tokenizer with custom cjk merges + unicode-norm NFC. Detok uses locale-aware bidi helper.
Sophia: do you have eval numbers? quick compare: BLEU zh->ar, baseline vs q5_k? and a precision/recall for named entities?
Maya: quick numbers from small testset (2k sents): BLEU baseline 27.8 -> q5_k 23.1 (-4.7). Named-entity exact-match (PERSON) baseline 94% -> q5_k 61%. Also observed ~12% of outputs with swapped paren orientation for Arabic lines.
Akira: thanks. can you try (a) quantize but disable kvcache-prefix, (b) run with per-sentence normalization off, (c) run a gnmt-style detok? we need to isolate whether it's quant kernel or prefix caching + detok interaction.
Maya: starting two jobs now: staging-lyra-8592a (q5_k + kvcache-prefix=off), staging-8592b (q5_k + kvcache-prefix=on + detok=legacy). will post logs.
ops-bot: CI job triggered -> test-eval/8592a (queued)
Jun: also run a tiny synthetic test: repeated short names to check embedding collisions, e.g., '李, 李, 李' and neutral contexts. if embedding rows collapsed after quant rounding it will show lower variance.
Liam: good call. If it's embedding aliasing, the fix could be per-row scaling or different quant bias handling for embedding matrix.
Sophia: if we reproduce, I'll prioritize an eval alert and rollback policy to avoid pushing lyra-q5_k to hosted until we have mitigation. current delta is too big for production. :rotating_light:
Maya: update: 8592a (kvcache-prefix off) ran — early glance: BLEU 27.4, PERSON-match 91%, paren flips dropped to ~1%. so major culprit seems interaction with kvcache-prefix when combined with q5_k.
Akira: excellent repro. can you collect kv cache dumps for a few examples (before/after) and attach hex diffs? we want to see whether cache slot indices or values are getting quantized incorrectly or byte-shifted.
Maya: uploading samples and small hex dump to staging-lyra-8592/attachments (will link in a sec).
ops-bot: Upload ready: https://redwood-staging/attachments/8592/kv-dumps.zip
Jun: next steps: (1) bisect kvcache-prefix commit range on runtime side, (2) try alternate quant backend (q5a) to see if kernel choice affects it, (3) add a unit test that asserts parity of detok for RTL punctuation with/without cache.
Liam: pinging infra to make a quick canary rollout block for lyra-q5_k until we confirm.
Sophia: thanks team. great triage. Maya — leave 8592a logs and sample diffs in thread when you can and we'll assign an owner for the bisect tomorrow. :thumbsup:
